content: Apple mint, also known as woolly mint, is scientifically classified as Mentha suaveolens. It is also referred to by its synonyms, including Mentha rotundifolia, Mentha macrostachya Ten., and Mentha insularis Req.. This plant belongs to the mint genus (Mentha) and is native to southern and western Europe as well as the western Mediterranean region. It is a herbaceous, upright perennial plant that is primarily cultivated for culinary purposes or as ground cover. Apple mint typically grows to a height of 40 to 100 centimeters and spreads through rhizomes, forming clonal colonies. Its foliage is light green, and the leaves are arranged oppositely on the stem. The leaves are sessile, oblong to nearly ovate in shape, measuring approximately 3 to 5 centimeters in length and 2 to 4 centimeters in width. The upper surface of the leaves is somewhat hairy, while the underside is downy. The edges of the leaves are serrated. During mid to late summer, the plant produces flowers that are light purple to pink in color. Apple mint is considered an attractive herb and is often grown as an ornamental plant. It is hardy and easy to cultivate, thriving in conditions ranging from full sun to partial shade. The leaves of apple mint are versatile and can be used to prepare apple mint jelly or as a flavoring ingredient in dishes such as apple mint couscous. Additionally, the leaves are commonly used to brew mint tea, as a garnish, or in salads. A notable cultivar of apple mint is pineapple mint (Mentha suaveolens 'Variegata'), which is distinguished by its leaves that are banded with white. Another hybrid derived from apple mint is grapefruit mint (Mentha suaveolens x piperata).
